notes: Analyst: the +0.60 delta is driven by pipeline artifacts, not fix quality — both runs converged on near-identical XAML approaches (Credential label + container/divider text + MaxHeight bump) since the bug spec prescribes acceptable directions. For cosmetic layout bugs, fix quality alone does not discriminate.

Analyst: 3 of the 6 baseline failures were by instruction (it was told not to push/PR, so PRE_FIX_SHA, branch convention, and PR assertions could not pass). The genuinely discriminating failures: no red-first regression test and no review pass — the baseline fixed the bug then reacted to a pre-existing test failure (test-after-fix); the skill wrote a dedicated regression test red-first that encodes the acceptance criterion.

Analyst: non-discriminating assertions (passed both runs): issue-comments-as-spec, verification-command-green, commit-references-issue, scope-respected. Baseline even matched conventional commit format unprompted — consider trimming these or reserving them as smoke checks.
Analyst: timing/token data unavailable — the harness did not supply total_tokens/duration_ms in completion notifications, so time and token columns are zeros.

Skill-improvement signal (deviations the with-skill run documented): (a) step 4 clean-tree check has no carve-out for unrelated dirty files though the open-PR path already carries the 'commit only the files the fix touches' rule; (b) /tdd 'confirm seams with user' has no unattended-mode guidance — run substituted the already-established test seam; (c) /review's subagent-dispatch fallback covers run_subagent-denied but not 'no subagent capability at all' — run invented the inline-axes adaptation; (d) step 8 leaves Closes #N placement in a new-PR body unspecified.
Analyst: positive signal — the run surfaced the milestone-branch auto-close caveat unprompted and flagged it for the /qa handoff; the pr-conventions pointer did its job.
